newsitem.title: ITALY: Olivetti ord shares open six pct up.
newsitem.headline: Olivetti ord shares open six pct up.

text.p: Ordinary shares in Italian information technology group Olivetti opened 6.19 percent higher at 705.0 lire per share in Milan.
Olivetti privileged shares were suspended for rising beyond a fluctuation limit, with quotations more than 14 percent up on the 1575 lire closing price, and saving shares rose 10 percent to 836 lire.
Olivetti announced late on Monday it was selling its loss-making personal computer division to a newly formed company Piedmont International in a deal worth 250 to 300 billion lire ($190.7 million).
Olivetti will have a 10 percent stake in Piedmont and the new company will license the Olivetti brand for 20 years and lease Olivetti's Scarmagno PC plant for four years.
Olivetti shares had been suspended on the bourse early on Monday prior to the announcement.
Turnover on Olivetti ordinary stock in pre-bourse opening trade was 24.5 million shares.

One trader said the market was viewing the deal and the amount Olivetti would gain from the operation positively but others said once the initial rush at the opening was out of the way the stock could retrace some of its gains.
"Now they are starting to think through what the real value of the group is without the costs of the PC activities," one said.
First trades at the start of the session at 0900 GMT showed ordinary shares trimming back the opening price gain to 5.29 percent up at 699.0 lire.
